Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Moderators started asking for this:

> As a moderator, I want to reuse my quiz at another conference, or share it with a colleague who runs Quizzy too.

The quiz page gets the "Export" link. It opens a page that shows the quiz as JSON inside a `<pre>` element (the only `<pre>` on the page), ready to copy.

`/moderate` gets the "Import quiz" button. It opens a page with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button. Importing always creates a new quiz, even if a quiz with the same title exists, and opens its page.

The format:

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `questions` and `options` keep their order.
- On import, `active` is optional (`true` by default), and `correct` is optional (`false` by default).
- The export always writes both, and it writes exactly these keys: the quiz title and its questions, nothing else. The export is only for moving quiz contents.
- Imported questions follow the same rules as the question form.

When the JSON is invalid or breaks a rule, the page shows an error and nothing is imported: not the quiz, not a part of its questions.

  "output_head": "# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Runtime & Deployment

- **Entrypoint**: `bin/serve` prepares SQLite (`bin/rails db:prepare`), compiles Propshaft assets (`bin/rails assets:clobber assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in the foreground listening on `0.0.0.0:${PORT}`.
- **Plain HTTP & Host Independence**: `config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`, `config.hosts.clear`, and `config.public_file_server.enabled = true` ensure the app works over plain HTTP on any conference network hostname without external dependencies.
- **Storage**: All persistent state lives under `storage/` (`storage/production.sqlite3`).
- **Health Check**: `GET /up` returns `200` without authentication.

## Authentication

- All moderator routes live under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`.
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic Authentication comparing against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` and `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]` using SHA-256 digests with `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`. Empty credentials are always rejected (`401`).

## Data Model (Release 1)

- `Quiz` (`quizzes`): `title` (required, whitespace-normalized). `has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `Question` (`questions`): `quiz_id`, `body` (required, whitespace-normalized), `position` (integer ordering), `active` (boolean, default `true`). `has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `Option` (`options`): `question_id`, `title` (required, whitespace-normalized), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (integer ordering).
- `Question#save_with_options` validates `body` and the filtered non-empty option rows (at least 2 options, at least 1 marked correct) before touching the database, preserving all submitted rows (including blanks) in memory if validation fails.
- `Question#move!(direction)` atomically swaps adjacent positions and normalizes `position` to `1..N` inside a transaction.

## Frontend & Design System

- **Assets**: `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` are sourced directly from `docs/mockups/`, compiled locally via Propshaft with zero external network calls.
- **Stimulus Controllers** (via Importmap, local vendored gems):
  - `option_rows_controller.js`: Dynamically adds/removes option rows and maintains contiguous numbering (`Option 1`, `Option 1 is correct`, etc.).
  - `question_active_controller.js`: Saves the `"Active"` checkbox immediately via `PATCH .../active` (`fetch` with `keepalive: true`), updating question numbering and active counts in place.
  - `preview_controller.js`: Runs the interactive quiz preview purely client-side over the quiz's active questions in order; preview answers are never persisted.
- **Accessibility & QA Compatibility**:
  - Lists use semantic `<ul>`/`<ol>` with each quiz/question in its own `<li>` containing its actions.
  - Icon-only buttons (`Move up`, `Move down`) use `aria-label` and `title` with `aria-hidden="true"` on glyphs.
  - Decorative CSS pseudo-elements (`+ ` on `Add option`, `Correct` on option checkboxes) use CSS Content Level 3 empty alt text (`content: "..." / ""`) so exact accessible names remain clean.
  - Destructive confirmations use native browser `confirm()` via Turbo (`data-turbo-confirm`).

## Notes for Future Releases (Live Runs, Big Screen, Phones)

- **Live Runs & Snapshots**: Currently `Question#save_with_options` replaces `options` via `delete_all` + `create!`. When live runs and participant answers are added, either snapshot questions/options per run or upsert options by `id` (and avoid deleting referenced options) so historical answers stay intact.
- **Real-time Updates**: ActionCable is enabled with the `async` adapter in single-process Puma (`config/cable.yml`), ready for broadcasting stage/question/reveal state to big screens and player phones without Redis.
- **Shared Styles**: `quizzy.css` already includes the `.screen`, `.cover`, `.lobby`, `.stage-option`, `.leaderboard`, `.play`, and `.response-*` classes for big-screen presentation, phone play, and moderator response summaries.

My test strategy involves making some real HTTP requests against the running `bin/serve` instance. I'll hit crucial endpoints like `/up`, `/moderate`, and `/moderate/import`. I'll also simulate an import of some JSON data that uses CSRF tokens, with Basic Auth, which has to be tested separately as it will require a different set of headers. bash -c '
set -euo pipefail

RAILS_ENV=production \
PORT=3000 \
SECRET_KEY_BASE=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=mod \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=pass \
bin/serve > /tmp/quizzy_serve.log 2>&1 &
SERVE_PID=$!

cleanup() {
  kill "$SERVE_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$SERVE_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f storage/production.sqlite3 storage/production.sqlite3-shm storage/production.sqlite3-wal /tmp/quizzy_cookies.txt /tmp/quizzy_serve.log
}
trap cleanup EXIT

for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  if curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:3000/up > /dev/null; then
    echo "Server ready!"
    break
  fi
  sleep 0.5
done

# 1. /up returns 200 without auth
status=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: conference.local:3000" http://127.0.0.1:3000/up)
echo "/up => $status"
test "$status" = "200"

# 2. /moderate/import returns 401 without auth
status=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:3000/moderate/import)
echo "/moderate/import (no auth) => $status"
test "$status" = "401"

# 3. /moderate returns 200 with auth and has Import quiz link
body=$(curl -sf -u mod:pass -H "Host: conference.local:3000" http://127.0.0.1:3000/moderate)
echo "$body" | grep -q "Import quiz"
echo "/moderate has Import quiz!"

# 4. GET /moderate/import returns 200 with auth, extract CSRF token, POST valid JSON
import_page=$(curl -sf -c /tmp/quizzy_cookies.txt -u mod:pass http://127.0.0.1:3000/moderate/import)
echo "$import_page" | grep -q "Quiz JSON"
csrf=$(echo "$import_page" | sed -n "s/.*name=\"csrf-token\" content=\"\([^\"]*\)\".*/\1/p" | head -n1)
test -n "$csrf"

  -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/moderate/import \
  --data-urlencode "authenticity_token=$csrf" \
  --data-urlencode "quiz_import[json]=$json_payload")
echo "POST /moderate/import => $loc"
echo "$loc" | grep -q "^303 "
quiz_url=$(echo "$loc" | awk "{print \$2}")

# 5. Quiz page has Export link
quiz_page=$(curl -sf -u mod:pass "$quiz_url")
echo "$quiz_page" | grep -q "Prod Smoke Quiz"
echo "$quiz_page" | grep -q "Export"

# 6. Export page has single <pre> with valid JSON
export_page=$(curl -sf -u mod:pass "${quiz_url}/export")
pre_count=$(echo "$export_page" | grep -o "<pre" | wc -l)
echo "pre_count => $pre_count"
test "$pre_count" = "1"
echo "$export_page" | grep -q "Prod Smoke Quiz"
echo "$export_page" | grep -q ""active": true"
echo "$export_page" | grep -q ""correct": false"

echo "ALL PRODUCTION SMOKE CHECKS PASSED!"
